record.original_question: Does there exist an ergodic automorphism whose absolutely continuous spectrum has finite multiplicity?

evidence.quote: Q4. Существует ли эргодические автоморфизмы с конечнократным абсолютно непрерывным спектром?
Эту задачу можно назвать ослабленной проблемой Банаха.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic Lebesgue probability space, and let $T:X\to X$ be an invertible measure-preserving transformation (an automorphism). The associated Koopman operator $U_T$ on $L^2_0(X,\mu)$ (the orthogonal complement of the constants) is a unitary operator, and by the spectral theorem it has a well-defined maximal spectral type (a measure class on the unit circle) and a multiplicity function. Say that $T$ has absolutely continuous spectrum of finite multiplicity if there is a Borel set $A$ of positive Lebesgue measure on the unit circle such that the restriction of $U_T$ to the spectral subspace associated with the absolutely continuous part of its spectrum is non-trivial, and the spectral multiplicity function is essentially bounded (i.e. finite almost everywhere with respect to Lebesgue measure) on the support of the absolutely continuous component.

Does there exist an ergodic automorphism $T$ of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ whose Koopman operator on $L^2_0(X,\mu)$ has a non-trivial absolutely continuous component of finite spectral multiplicity?
artifact.status_search_result: This is a weakened form of Banach's classical problem (which asks for an ergodic finite measure-preserving automorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum). The original Banach problem remains open for finite measure-preserving transformations; a positive answer is known only in the conservative σ-finite (infinite measure) setting. The weakened version, asking merely for finite multiplicity of the absolutely continuous component, also appears to remain open in the probability-preserving setting, as no construction is recorded in current surveys of spectral theory of dynamical systems.

status_evidence.title: Spectral theory of dynamical systems (Kanigowski–Lemańczyk survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of spectral problems in ergodic theory discussing Banach's problem and finite multiplicity Lebesgue components.
status_evidence.claim: Banach's problem in the finite measure setting remains open, and constructions yielding Lebesgue components of finite multiplicity are limited.

status_evidence.title: Spectral ergodic Banach problem and flat polynomials (arXiv:1508.06439)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a conservative ergodic infinite measure-preserving transformation with simple Lebesgue spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Banach's problem is answered affirmatively in the infinite-measure (conservative) setting; the finite-measure version remains open.
